draft.title: International crime
card: International crime is crime that goes beyond one country's own law. There are two main kinds, and they differ in what makes them international.
acts that international law treats as serious wrongs, such as genocide and war crimes. They are international because of what the act is, not where it happens.
crime that crosses national borders, such as drug trafficking and cybercrime. It is international because the offending, the people or the effects reach more than one country.
A crime can be one kind without the other. A drug ring that moves cargo between countries is transnational, but drug trafficking is not genocide or a war crime.
draft.remember: Some crimes are international by their nature. Others are international because they cross borders.

a.q: Which crime is a transnational crime?
opts: A cyber attack on a bank in Australia launched from Romania
A fight between two people in a Sydney park
A theft from a shop in Newcastle by a local
A break-in at a house in Perth by a neighbour
a.why: The attacker and the victim are in different countries, so the crime crosses a border. The other three happen between people in one place and one country, so they are not transnational.
a.clue: Look for the crime where the offender and victim are in different countries.

b.q: A group of soldiers deliberately kills civilians in a war, all inside one country. Why is this an international crime?
opts: International law treats the act itself as a serious wrong
It is transnational because the soldiers carried weapons
It is transnational because news of it spread overseas
It is only international if the victims cross a border
b.why: War crimes are crimes against international law because of the nature of the act, so no border crossing is needed. The tempting option says the victims must cross a border, but that test applies to transnational crime, not to crimes against international law.
b.clue: Ask whether the act is international because of what it is or because of where it goes.

a.best: A cyber attack on a bank in Australia launched from Romania

b.best: International law treats the act itself as a serious wrong
